I've studied the app and some reference designs. Before I build anything, you need to pick one of three directions.

**What the app does today, which every direction keeps:** it lists seed loans (variety, borrower, date lent, on loan or returned), filters them by variety name as you type, and has a button to mark a loan returned. The redesign changes how it looks and how it's laid out. It doesn't change what it does.

**Research:** I looked at reference components on 21st.dev. Refero and Mobbin aren't connected, so I didn't look at any finished products. I saved the preview images to `.playwright-mcp/refs/`. I couldn't add that folder to `.git/info/exclude` because the edit wasn't permitted, so leave it out of any commit or add it to the exclude file yourself.

---

### A — The Lending Ledger (built closely on one reference)
`Energy 1 · Density 3 · Motion 1 · Fidelity high`

- **References:**
  - [Data Table (uvain)](https://21st.dev/@uvain/components/data-table-bulk-actions) ([preview](https://cdn.21st.dev/uvain/data-table-bulk-actions/default/preview.1790665384272-34d87f4a-e7c2-41b4-b950-1331ee58df77.jpg)): a titled panel with a one-line summary, a toolbar row, then a table with clear lines between rows.
  - [Streaming Data Rows](https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/streaming-data-rows) ([preview](https://cdn.21st.dev/rmahammad/streaming-data-rows/default/preview.1790069508080-60d6e586-78d5-44b1-9a7e-05fb8b3d5930.png)): status labels that pair an icon with a word, and a brief highlight on a row when it changes.
- **What it takes from them:**
  - **Composition:** the Data Table's panel → summary line ("Spring 2026 · 3 packets lent · 2 still out") → search → table with columns Variety / Grower / Out since / Status / action.
  - **Hierarchy:** variety names in heavy type, borrowers in regular weight, dates in fixed-width numerals (Data Table).
  - **Spacing:** generous row height with thin dividers (Data Table).
  - **Interaction:** search filters as you type; a "No varieties match '…' — Clear search" message when nothing matches (Data Table); "Mark returned" sits in the row itself.
  - **Motion:** a row briefly highlights when marked returned, and the highlight is switched off for people who turn off animation (Streaming Rows).
  - **Visual treatment:** neutral surfaces, with status shown as an icon plus a word, never colour alone. The colours change from invoice-app defaults to soil and leaf tones.
- **Look:** one clean sans-serif typeface with fixed-width numerals, high contrast, one deep-green accent, square corners. On phones, each row becomes a two-line entry.
- **Signature:** the summary line reads like a volunteer's handwritten tally in the ledger.
- **Avoids:** cards, decoration, the purple button.
- **Tradeoff:** the safest and fastest to scan, but the least personal. It could be any lending tracker.

### B — The Seed Tin
`Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 2 · Fidelity medium`

- **References:**
  - Things volunteers already handle: paper seed packets, a library date-due slip, a rubber date stamp.
  - [Folder Card](https://21st.dev/@uvain/components/folder-card) (stacked silhouette).
  - [Card Status List](https://21st.dev/@isaiahbjork/components/card-status-list) ([preview](https://cdn.21st.dev/user_2tkbBPFWYn8YMjZNHwgIuP3yzvd/card-status-list/default/preview.1750810684673.png)): an item visibly changing state in place.
- **Layout:** each loan is a seed-packet envelope. Packets are split into two groups: "Still out in gardens" (the main area) and "Back in the tin" (a smaller, quieter row).
- **Look:** warm kraft-paper and seed-ink colours. Variety names in a serif display face, as on a printed packet; dates set like a stamp ("OUT · 14 MAR 26"); grower name on a little slip.
- **Signature:** pressing "Mark returned" lands a RETURNED rubber stamp on the packet, which then moves into the tin. With animation turned off, it simply swaps.
- **Avoids:** generic app cards, pill-shaped badges, a grey page background.
- **Tradeoff:** warm and memorable, but less dense. It gets crowded past about 60 loans.

### C — The Season Almanac
`Energy 4 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity low`

- **References:**
  - [Returns Calendar](https://21st.dev/@ssychui/components/returns-calendar) ([preview](https://cdn.21st.dev/user_3CdJgTW8geRShR3gegqAjY0JB3B/returns-calendar/default/preview.1787345382939.png)): month columns with labelled cells.
  - A gardener's planting almanac, and the rows of a seed-saving record.
- **Layout:** the whole screen is the growing season, laid across from March to October. Each loan is a growth line starting on its lend date. An unreturned loan's line keeps growing toward harvest. A returned one closes with a seed mark. Search highlights matching lines and dims the rest. On phones, the season runs down the page.
- **Look:** an almanac-style large serif heading with a "week 27 of the season" marker, a thin grid, and one colour per crop family.
- **Signature:** seeing at a glance which seed has been out longest this season.
- **Avoids:** tables and cards entirely.
- **Tradeoff:** the most distinctive, but the most experimental. With only a few loans it looks sparse, and it leans hard on dates.

---

Pick A, B, C, or a mix (for example "A's layout with B's look"). Once you choose, I'll write down the pre-build check and then build, test it in the browser on phone and desktop, and send it for review.

runs.reply:
I haven't changed any code yet. A full redesign has an open visual direction, so I need you to pick one before I build. Here are three, based on the current app (a header, a search box and a grid of identical white cards, with three loans in the data) and on four shipped components I found on 21st.dev and looked at.

The job, as I understand it: a volunteer at the library desk needs to see what's still out, who has it and for how long. ### A — The Ledger (desk register)
`Energy 2 · Density 3 · Motion 1 · Fidelity medium`

- **References:**
  - [Records Table](https://21st.dev/@theshanelevine/components/records-table): a sticky first column, tag chips that each carry a small dot and a count in the footer row.
  - [Streaming Data Rows](https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/streaming-data-rows): status labels that pair an icon with text, so status doesn't rely on colour alone.
- **Layout:** one full-width register of loans, not cards. The columns are packet, borrower, date out, days out, saved seed and action. Above it sits a strip of season totals (on loan, overdue, seed returned) that also work as filters. On mobile each row becomes a two-line entry, not a card.
- **Look:** warm off-white paper with fine ruled lines. A serif for variety names, tabular figures for dates, and one deep green accent used only for the action.
- **Signature:** a "days out" column that gets darker as a loan ages, so long loans stand out at a glance.
- **Avoids:** cards, a hero area, decorative charts.
- **Tradeoff:** it's the quietest of the three. It works well as a tool but isn't very expressive.

### B — The Seed Drawer (the physical catalogue)
`Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 2 · Fidelity low`

- **References:** these come from the library's own world, not from shipped products:
  - Seed packets: the variety name as the hero, plus a lot number and date.
  - The card-catalogue drawer.
  - The borrower's slip.
  - The Timeline component's [grouping by day](https://21st.dev/@kuratlielia/components/timeline), used here for grouping by month borrowed.
- **Layout:** loans are drawn as packets: tall cards with a printed-label header, the borrower's name written on a slip, and a stamped "RETURNED" mark. Packets are grouped into drawers by month borrowed, with a running log of what was lent and returned beside them.
- **Look:** kraft and cream tones, bold condensed type for variety names, and a monospace "lot number".
- **Signature:** marking a loan returned stamps the packet, a short animated press that doesn't play if reduced motion is on.
- **Avoids:** generic dashboard chrome, plain white-on-grey cards.
- **Tradeoff:** shows fewer loans per screen. It gets crowded past about 40 active loans.

### C — The Season Board (reference-led)
`Energy 4 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high`

- **Reference:** [Kanban Board by uvain](https://21st.dev/@uvain/components/kanban-board) ([video](https://cdn.21st.dev/user_3AAcYdXInfTxs5akkUBbQIUQdhX/kanban-board/default/video.1789061691737.mp4)). It's built for real data, and its pointer-based drag works on a trackpad and a phone.

  - **Hierarchy:** status comes from the column, so cards don't need badges.
  - **Spacing rhythm:** its card spacing, made a little looser.
  - **Interaction:** pointer drag between columns.
  - **Motion:** its drag and lift.
  - **Visual treatment:** not taken; it gets a botanical palette with a different colour per stage.

- **Avoids:** tables and filter chips.
- **Tradeoff:** it's the most to build, and dragging is slower than one click when you're processing returns in bulk.

directions_self_scored.heading: ### A: Seed packet stubs (based closely on two references)

runs.reply:
I've finished the research. Before I write any UI code, you need to pick a direction. The project's frontend process requires that step for an open-ended redesign.

**Scope.** Seedkeep is one screen: a search by variety, a list of loans (variety, borrower, date out, status), a "Return" action on each open loan, and a footer. All three directions keep exactly that. Anything new I suggest below is marked *optional* and won't be built unless you ask for it.

**Research note.** Refero and Mobbin aren't connected, so I haven't looked at any real shipped products. The references below are 21st.dev components; I opened each preview image, and they're saved in `.design/refs/`.

---

### A: Seed packet stubs (based closely on two references)
`Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high`

- **References:**
  - [Admit One Ticket](https://21st.dev/@larsen66/components/admit-one-ticket): a perforated stub with punched corners, a grainy two-tone surface, a big name set in type, and a stub rotated sideways.
  - [Filter Grid](https://21st.dev/@ddoemonn/components/filter-grid): cards that reflow smoothly when the filter changes.
- **What it takes from them:**
  - **Layout:** each loan is a seed packet, with the variety name set large. A perforated stub on the right shows the borrower and "out since".
  - **Hierarchy:** variety first, then borrower, then date.
  - **Spacing:** generous packets, with tight type inside the stub.
  - **Interaction:** on open loans, the stub is the "Return" button. Searching reflows the packets as in Filter Grid.
  - **Motion:** returning a packet tears off its stub, the packet settles into a muted state, and the grid reflows.
  - **Surface:** grain texture and two-tone ink on kraft paper, no shadows.
- **Look:** a condensed display face for variety names and a mono face for dates. Kraft paper and dark soil colours, with one ink colour per crop family. Squared packets with punched corners.
- **Signature:** the stub tear when a packet is returned.
- **Avoids:** white cards on grey, pill badges, and indigo buttons.
- **Tradeoff:** large packets mean fewer loans visible at once. That's fine for dozens of loans, but it gets long with hundreds.

### B: Circulation ledger
`Energy 2 · Density 3 · Motion 2 · Fidelity low`

- **References:** objects from the seed library's own world: a library due-date card, a botanical seed catalogue, and a rubber date stamp. The [Revision Timeline](https://21st.dev/@saurabh-2607/components/great-ui-revision-timeline) only calibrates the mono date treatment.
- **Layout:** one ruled ledger page instead of a card grid. Variety is set in a serif, borrower in italics, and dates in a mono column. On mobile, each row becomes a two-line entry.
- **Look:** warm paper, ink-black text and hairline rules. The only colour is a red-violet stamp.
- **Signature:** returning a loan presses a "RETURNED · 3 OCT" rubber stamp across the row, slightly rotated. The status is shown in words as well as colour.
- **Avoids:** cards, shadows and rounded corners.
- **Tradeoff:** it's the calmest of the three and the easiest to scan. It leans on typography more than on drama.

### C: Season bed
`Energy 4 · Density 3 · Motion 4 · Fidelity medium`

- **References:**
  - Revision Timeline: a tick-mark scale and a scrubbing date marker.
  - [diceui Stack](https://21st.dev/@diceui/components/stack): stacked items that fan out (used for the mobile layout).
- **Layout:** the growing season, March to October, runs across the screen as a field. Each loan is a row, with a stem that grows from its "out" date to today, so loans out the longest stand tallest. A "today" line runs down through the field. Search fades the rows that don't match.
- **Look:** dark soil background with chalk-green stems, and a heavy grotesque typeface for variety names.
- **Signature:** returning seed "harvests" the stem, which closes it off with a seed-head mark.
- **Mobile:** the rows become a vertical stack, and the stems become horizontal progress lines.
- **Tradeoff:** it's the most memorable and the most work to build. The timeline also takes up space even with only 3 loans.

---

*Optional, can be added to any direction:* All / On loan / Returned filter chips with counts.

Pick **A**, **B**, **C**, or a mix (for example, "B's ledger with A's stub tear"), and I'll write the plan and build it. If you'd rather it follow a particular product or page, name it.

Seedkeep is used by volunteers at a seed-library desk. They need to see what's out and who has it, and mark packets as returned. The app currently has three loans, a search box and a "Return" button.

---

### A — Seed Ledger
`Energy 2 · Density 3 · Motion 2 · Fidelity medium`

- **References:**
  - Records Table — https://21st.dev/@theshanelevine/components/records-table. I'd take the compact rows, a sticky variety column and a count footer.
  - Streaming Data Rows — https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/streaming-data-rows. I'd take the status chips with icons and the brief highlight on a row that just changed.
- **Look:** a warm off-white page like a library logbook. Variety names in a serif font, dates and day counts in monospace. Each row has a status chip with a glyph and a word, so status never depends on colour alone. A summary strip shows "6 on loan · 2 overdue for seed return · 14 returned this season".
- **Signature:** when you mark a packet returned, its row briefly lights up green, the chip changes to "Returned ✓", and the counts update.
- **Avoids:** card grids and big header areas.
- **Tradeoff:** the most efficient for volunteers, but the least memorable. It's a well-made table.

### B — Packet Drawer (closely follows its references)
`Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high`

- **References:**
  - Stacked Activity Cards — https://21st.dev/@spydiecy/components/stacked-activity-cards
  - Dice UI Stack — https://21st.dev/@diceui/components/stack
- **What it borrows from them:**
  - **Layout:** loans sit in stacks of cards that fan open (Activity Cards). There's one stack per status: *On loan*, *Seed due back*, *Returned*.
  - **Hierarchy:** the top card shows the variety, borrower and date. The cards behind it show only their edges (Stack).
  - **Spacing:** a tight overlap when closed and roomy spacing when open (both references).
  - **Interaction:** click or press Enter on a stack to open it. Each card has a "Mark returned" button (Activity Cards' "Show all" toggle).
  - **Motion:** the open/close animation with scaling and shifting cards. Marking a card returned slides it across into the *Returned* stack. I'll watch both reference videos before building.
  - **Surface:** layered shadows and depth; colours are my own.
- **Look:** each card looks like a seed packet, with a crop-coloured band and a stamped "out" date. The background is a deep soil colour.
- **Signature:** a returned packet physically moving from one stack to the other.
- **Avoids:** tables and filter sidebars.
- **Tradeoff:** with 100+ loans, scanning everything is slower than in a table. Search stays as a backup.

### C — Season Almanac
`Energy 4 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity medium`

- **References:**
  - Filterable Blog Index — https://21st.dev/@olewandowski1/components/blog-3. I'd take its large featured item over a grid and its filter pills.
  - Proposal Tracker Card — https://21st.dev/@kavikatiyar/components/tracker-card-1. I'd take its vertical step timeline.
- **Look:** an almanac page with a large serif headline ("Spring 2026 loans") and a season timeline from sowing to harvest to seed return, with each loan placed along it. A featured panel shows the loan that has been out longest, with a large "Mark returned" button. Filter pills: All / On loan / Returned. Each crop family gets its own colour, always paired with a text label.
- **Signature:** the season timeline, where each loan's marker moves as the season goes on.
- **Avoids:** a dashboard look and same-sized card grids.
- **Tradeoff:** the most distinctive option, but the timeline is new territory. It takes the most build effort and needs the most care on mobile.

---

**My recommendation is B.** It's the strongest of the three that still keeps the main task (find a loan, mark it returned) one click away. A would suit you if desk speed matters more than personality.

### B: Packet Wall (built on the references)
`Energy 3 · Density 2 · Motion 3 · Fidelity high`

  - Hierarchy: variety name, then borrower, then date as fine print (Ticket).
  - Spacing: tight fine-print blocks against open space (Ticket).
  - Interaction: hover or focus tilts the packet; Return flips it to a "seed saved" back face (Ticket).
  - Motion: tilt, and a short ink re-spray when the stamp lands (Ticket).
  - Treatment: paper grain, line-engraved botanical ornament, two-ink print (Ticket).
- **Look:** printed seed packets on a deep soil-coloured shelf. Each variety gets its own ink colour (tomato red, bean violet, cucumber yellow-green), with cream paper and black type.

- **Tradeoff:** less information fits on screen; with a few hundred loans it would need grouping.

`Energy 4 · Density 3 · Motion 4 · Fidelity medium`

- **Signature:** Return throws the packet off the timeline into a "Saved seed" bin that keeps a running count.
- **Avoids:** static lists, neutral greys.
- **Tradeoff:** the most striking and the most complex. On mobile the season strip has to become a vertical timeline, and the motion needs careful reduced-motion fallbacks.

---

**Optional extras** (not part of the current app, and I'd add them only if you want): status filter tabs with counts, an undo after Return, and showing how long each loan has been out.

- **Signature:** the packet physically going back into the drawer when its saved seed comes back.
- **Avoids:** generic cards, a static grid, the old indigo buttons.

# Proposal Q5

### A — The Ledger (desk register)


- **References:**
  - [Records Table](https://21st.dev/@theshanelevine/components/records-table): a sticky first column, tag chips that each carry a small dot and a count in the footer row.
  - [Streaming Data Rows](https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/streaming-data-rows): status labels that pair an icon with text, so status doesn't rely on colour alone.

- **Look:** warm off-white paper with fine ruled lines. A serif for variety names, tabular figures for dates, and one deep green accent used only for the action.
- **Signature:** a "days out" column that gets darker as a loan ages, so long loans stand out at a glance.
- **Avoids:** cards, a hero area, decorative charts.
- **Tradeoff:** it's the quietest of the three. It works well as a tool but isn't very expressive.

# Proposal Q2

### A — The circulation ledger


Every loan is one row in a ledger, so a volunteer at the desk can scan, search and check in quickly.
- **References:**
  - [Records Table](https://21st.dev/@theshanelevine/components/records-table): a sticky first column, a count in the footer, and tag chips that carry a small dot.
  - [Streaming Data Rows](https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/streaming-data-rows): status pills that pair an icon with the label, so status isn't shown by colour alone, and a brief highlight on a row that changes.
- **What it takes from each reference:**
  - **Layout:** a full-width table with the variety pinned as the first column (Records Table).
  - **What reads first:** quiet column headers and strong variety names (both references).
  - **Spacing:** dense rows split by thin hairline rules (Records Table).
  - **Interaction:** check-in from the row itself, with the row briefly highlighted when it changes (Streaming Rows).
  - **Motion:** only that row highlight (Streaming Rows).
  - **Look:** chips with an icon or dot, recoloured from the references' SaaS blues to garden colours.
- **Visual character:** a monospaced font for dates and a plain sans for names. Warm off-white "ledger paper" with hairline rules. One deep green for actions. Square corners.
- **Signature:** the footer tallies the season, e.g. "3 packets lent · 1 home · 2 still in the ground".
- **Avoids:** cards, shadows, large headers.
- **Tradeoff:** it's efficient but plain, and on a phone the rows become stacked blocks.

- preview of https://21st.dev/@theshanelevine/components/records-table: `$PROBE_ROOT/blind2/Q2/A1.jpg`

- preview of https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/streaming-data-rows: `$PROBE_ROOT/blind2/Q2/A2.jpg`



### B — The season board


Two lanes, **In the ground** and **Seed came home**. Checking a packet in moves it across, so the board shows how the season is going at a glance.
- **References:** [Kanban Board](https://21st.dev/@uvain/components/kanban-board), taking its lane headers with counts and its cards with a metadata row along the bottom. I'm not taking drag-and-drop: a labelled button is easier to use with a keyboard and on a phone.
- **Visual character:** a rounded humanist sans. Lane backgrounds in soil and leaf tones. Each card has a "days out" counter, which is how long the packet has been lent.
- **Signature:** when you check a packet in, the card slides across to the other lane, so the animation shows what changed. With reduced motion turned on, it switches lanes instantly.
- **Avoids:** a dashboard look with metric tiles.
- **Tradeoff:** it holds fewer loans per screen than A, and on a phone the lanes stack vertically.

- preview of https://21st.dev/@uvain/components/kanban-board: `$PROBE_ROOT/blind2/Q2/B1.jpg`



### C — The packet drawer


Every loan looks like a physical seed envelope with a library due-date slip.
- **References:**
  - [Ticket Confirmation Card](https://21st.dev/@ravikatiyar162/components/ticket-confirmation-card), for the notched, perforated slip shape.
  - Things the library's volunteers already handle: kraft-paper seed envelopes, rubber date stamps, and the date-due card in a library book.
- **Visual character:** a serif font for variety names, typewriter-style dates, kraft and cream paper colours, and stamp-red ink for statuses.
- **Signature:** when you check a packet in, a "RETURNED · 3 OCT 2026" rubber stamp lands on its slip.
- **Avoids:** looking like a SaaS app, with neutral grey and a single accent colour.
- **Tradeoff:** it's the most memorable and the most fun to use, but it fits the fewest loans on screen and is the slowest to scan once there are dozens.

- preview of https://21st.dev/@ravikatiyar162/components/ticket-confirmation-card: `$PROBE_ROOT/blind2/Q2/C1.jpg`

# Proposal Q6

### A — "The seed drawer" (based closely on two references)


- **References:**
  - Tracker Card (https://21st.dev/@ravikatiyar162/components/tracker-card): the item itself is the main image, with a large status headline and a monospace ID line.
  - Stacked Activity Cards (https://21st.dev/@spydiecy/components/stacked-activity-cards): a collapsed stack with a depth shadow that springs open into a list.
- **What it borrows:**
  - *Layout:* each loan is a seed-packet card, laid out like the Tracker Card. Loans are grouped into two stacks that open and close: "Out in gardens" and "Back in the drawer".
  - *Hierarchy:* the status is the headline ("With R. Okafor"), above a monospace line with the packet number and lend date.
  - *Spacing:* generous spacing inside each card, tight spacing between stacked cards (from Stacked Activity Cards).
  - *Interaction:* opening and collapsing stacks. Search opens every stack and narrows them as you type.
  - *Motion:* stacks fan out and close up with a spring. Pressing Return slides the packet out of the "out" stack and onto the drawer stack.
  - *Visual treatment:* layered depth and soft shadows, on kraft paper instead of white.
- **Look:** kraft paper and ink. Each packet is a CSS-drawn envelope with a colour band for its crop (deep purple for Cherokee Purple, lemon for the cucumber). Headlines in a condensed serif, dates in monospace.
- **Signature:** a returned packet visibly files itself back into the drawer.
- **Avoids:** white cards on grey, a single flat grid, the indigo button.
- **Main cost:** a stack hides how many loans are inside until it's opened. Each stack needs a clear count and a "show all" option.

- preview of https://21st.dev/@spydiecy/components/stacked-activity-cards: `$PROBE_ROOT/blind2/Q6/A2.jpg`



### B — "Growing-season calendar"


- **Reference:** Animated List (https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/animated-list), for how rows come in, leave and reorder when the search filters them.
- **Layout:** one season timeline running March to October. Each loan is a bar from its lend date to today. A returned loan's bar ends in a small seed mark, while an open loan's bar keeps growing toward a "today" line. Long open loans stand out at a glance, which a card grid can't show.
- **Look:** a field notebook in green ink on linen. Serif variety names, hand-ruled month gridlines, muted earthy colours, and status shown as text as well as colour.
- **Signature:** the "today" line, with overdue loans literally reaching past where the season should end.
- **Avoids:** a dashboard look, stat tiles, card grids.
- **Main cost:** it's the calmest of the three and the most chart-like. On mobile the timeline has to collapse to a vertical list.

### C — "A hand of packets"


- **References:**

- **Look:** bold, flat colour blocks. Every crop gets a saturated full-card colour and an oversized display face, like printed seed-packet art.
- **Signature:** dragging through the fan, and returned packets flipping over to show a "seed saved" back.
- **Avoids:** neutral backgrounds, small type, list-first layouts.
- **Main cost:** it's the least efficient for a volunteer processing many returns. Once the library grows past about 20 packets, the list underneath does the real work.

# Proposal Q1

### A — The Packet Drawer *(built on references)*


- **References:**
  - [Layered Stack](https://21st.dev/@paceui/components/layered-stack): a stack of slightly tilted cards that spreads out into a neat grid on hover.
  - [Wallet Card](https://21st.dev/@educalvolpz/components/wallet-card): stacked cards that look physical, with real depth and a fixed set of labelled fields.
- **Adapts:**
  - *Composition:* each loan is a seed packet. Packets still on loan sit in a loose stack that spreads into a grid (Layered Stack).
  - *Hierarchy:* the variety name is set large on the packet face, with borrower and date as small labelled fields, like "CARD HOLDER / VALID THRU" on Wallet Card.
  - *Spacing:* packets overlap loosely in the stack, then align tightly in the grid.
  - *Interaction:* hover or focus lifts a packet. "Return" slides it into a separate "Back in the drawer" shelf.
  - *Motion:* the packets spread from stack to grid, and a returned packet slides across to the shelf.
  - *Visual treatment:* layered shadows and cards with real depth.
- **Look:** saturated packet art on a dark soil background. Each variety gets its own colour (Cherokee Purple is a deep aubergine, Lemon cucumber is yellow). A condensed display typeface for names, with small caps for the fields.
- **Signature:** pressing Return makes the packet fly into the drawer, and the drawer's count goes up.
- **Avoids:** flat cards, the indigo accent, white on grey.
- **Tradeoff:** it is the most theatrical option, and it gets busy beyond about 40 loans.

- preview of https://21st.dev/@paceui/components/layered-stack: `$PROBE_ROOT/blind2/Q1/A1.jpg`

- preview of https://21st.dev/@educalvolpz/components/wallet-card: `$PROBE_ROOT/blind2/Q1/A2.jpg`



### B — Season Almanac


- **References:**
  - [Phyllotaxis Bloom](https://21st.dev/@daiwiikharihar/components/phyllotaxis-bloom): a sunflower seed spiral, used here as a progress figure.
  - [Animated List](https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/animated-list): rows that move smoothly when the list is filtered or reordered.
- **Structure:** a large top band shows the growing season from March to October, with each loan drawn as a bar starting on the day it went out. Below it is a list you can search, which reflows smoothly as you type.
- **Look:** bold flat blocks of colour on a bright background, using garden colours (tomato red, bean violet, cucumber yellow), with large editorial headings.
- **Signature:** a seed-head spiral fills in with each packet returned, showing how much of the season's seed has come back.
- **Avoids:** packets drawn as cards, and dark backgrounds.
- **Tradeoff:** the timeline takes up space at the top, so on a phone it has to shrink to a thin strip.

### C — Herbarium Ledger


- **References:**
  - [Filter Grid](https://21st.dev/@ddoemonn/components/filter-grid): filter buttons that show a count for each option.
  - [Animated List](https://21st.dev/@rmahammad/components/animated-list): smooth reflow.
- **Structure:** two sections, "In the ground" (on loan) and "Back in the library" (returned). A returned loan moves from the first to the second.
- **Look:** dark ink on cream paper, with thin botanical rules and a serif for variety names. Each loan is written out like a herbarium specimen label.

Q1.composition_why: A is a stack of packet cards that spreads into a grid, with a separate drawer shelf; B is a season-timeline band over a reflowing list, with a seed-spiral progress figure; C is two ruled sections of specimen-label entries.
Q1.register_why: A uses saturated packet colours on dark soil with a condensed display face; B uses bold flat garden-colour blocks on a bright ground with editorial headings; C uses dark ink on cream with a serif and botanical rules.

Q2.composition_why: A is a dense full-width table, B is a two-lane kanban that cards move across, and C is a collection of envelope-and-slip cards, so each has a different main unit and eye path.
Q2.register_why: A (warm off-white ledger paper with mono dates) and C (kraft and cream with serif, typewriter type and stamp red) share a paper-and-ink register; only B, a rounded sans on soil and leaf lanes, steps away from it, and B is still a recoloured SaaS kanban.

Q3.composition_why: A is a panel, toolbar and table; B is packet envelopes split between a main 'out' area and a smaller 'tin' row; C turns the whole screen into a March-to-October season with growth lines.
Q3.register_why: A is a neutral single-sans invoice-table register, but B (kraft paper, serif packet type, stamps) and C (almanac serif heading, thin grid) both sit in a printed-paper, serif register.

Q4.composition_why: A is a season strip over a searchable list with a detail panel; B fans packets across the top with a returned pile below; C is a tabbed card-catalogue drawer of index cards in tight rows.
Q4.register_why: A is dark green on off-white with a clay accent and serif headings; B uses saturated full-colour packets with bold sans on cream; C puts brown-paper cards on deep pine green with typewriter type and stamp red.

Q5.composition_why: A is a full-width register table under a strip of totals, B groups tall packet cards into monthly drawers beside a running log, and C is a four-column life-cycle kanban with drag.
Q5.register_why: A (warm ruled off-white with a serif) and B (kraft and cream with condensed and mono type) are both paper registers, and C is a kanban recoloured with a botanical palette, not a distinct visual world.

Q6.composition_why: B is a full-screen season timeline, but A (two springing packet stacks) and C (a fanned hand of packets around a focused card) both make layered packet cards the main unit.
Q6.register_why: A (kraft paper and ink, condensed serif) and B (green ink on linen, serif, hand-ruled lines) share a paper-and-ink register; only C, with flat saturated colour blocks and an oversized display face, is distinct.
